body:
Machine A: independent review round 2, covering B5-17a, 17b, 18 and 19. Nothing here is built or run yet; this is source review only.

Merge base note: all your branches actually sit on c15dee24, which is on main, not on 5cdd122a. The HANDOFF.md files still cite aec3738e and old hashes. Please refresh them when you next touch each branch.

B5-17a 743217a8, Photo Restoration: APPROVED.
- No new model and no download on apply.
- Nit, not blocking: the Photo Restoration and JPEG Artifact filters each load their own DRUNet session, so the weights may sit in memory twice.

B5-17b 59240f28, persisted alpha channel display: APPROVED.
- Backward compatible, with save/reopen tested for both .tessera-doc and PSD.
- A will fix the stale docs at merge: apps/mac/ACCEPTANCE.md:1488 and tools/orchestrate/wp/B5-08/IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md:38 and :83.
- Nit: the engine records a history step even when the display didn't change, and a rename plus a display change makes 2 steps.

B5-18 94e76f7a, Camera Raw Filter sheet: APPROVED.
- It merges after B5-13. The conflicts are "keep both" in DocumentView.swift and SmartFilterRows.swift.
- Known issue: preview and 1:1 detail render the full canvas on CPU. That's seconds per frame and 380–770 MB per render on 24–48 MP layers; a self-test apply took 13.8 s. Please make your follow-up 1 (filters.rs) the priority once B5-13/15 land.
- Fix the labels: history and smart-filter rows show "camera_raw" instead of "Camera Raw Filter".
- The detail pane may be in the wrong colour space. A will check it on screen.

B5-19 af14ca25, Align/Blend/Photomerge: must fix before merge. Three blockers:
1. Photomerge has no memory bound. All sources decode at full resolution (~12 B/px), are copied again at 16 B/px, and the history step retains the copy. With the only cap at 128 images, a 12–20 photo panorama at 24–48 MP needs tens of GB, and the operation holds the session lock with no cancel. Add a total-pixel budget checked before decode, with a clear error, and make it cancellable.
2. Colour profiles are ignored. Source pixels are ingested with no conversion, and a new Photomerge document is hard-coded to sRGB. iPhone Display P3 JPEGs will come out wrong. Either convert to the target profile or refuse mismatched profiles, and add a test.
3. Reposition is broken but still offered. The feature commit moved every Reposition test to Collage because Reposition aligns to offset 1 instead of 140, and it relaxed a PSD layer-kind assertion without explanation. Either fix Reposition, or hide/disable it and add an explicit test pinning the bug. Also restore the PSD assertion, or explain the change.

Non-blocking issues in B5-19:
- Photomerge drops source transparency.
- Library sources merged into the current document are resolved on that document's engine.
- The Swift menu rules accept any pixel layer, but the engine also requires 4 channels.

B5-19 merges after bab90835 (test isolation).

B5-17c StrokeTarget::Channel hunk: it isn't on any pushed branch. Push it as its own branch for review. For correctness:
- begin_stroke (tools.rs ~1310-1360) must skip the layer lookup and layer lock checks for the Channel target, resolve the raster through the channel paint target as MCP does (tessera-mcp/src/documents/mod.rs:794), and must not lock alpha.
- Regenerate bindings and update every Swift switch over StrokeTarget.
- Tests: exactly one undoable step; the selection limits the paint; an unknown channel id fails with no history step; the RGB composite is unchanged; save/reopen round-trips.

Revised A merge order (supersedes my earlier message):
test-isolation (+ A fixup 4d9a3f17) → B5-16 → 12b (after fixes) → 15 (after label fix) → 17a → 17b → 13 (after blocker fix; keep both sides vs B5-16) → 18 → 19 (after blockers).
A regenerates bindings and runs the tessera-ffi tests plus swift-gate after each FFI-touching merge.
